related_questions.question: What is the vaccine recommended for teens?

text_blocks.snippet: Adolescents (ages 11-18) need several vaccines to protect them from preventable diseases. Key recommendations include the Tdap vaccine (tetanus, diphtheria, and pertussis), meningococcal vaccines (MenACWY and MenB), and the HPV vaccine. Annual influenza (flu) vaccines are also crucial for this age group.
snippet_highlighted_words: Tdap vaccine (tetanus, diphtheria, and pertussis), meningococcal vaccines (MenACWY and MenB), and the HPV vaccine

list.snippet: Tdap: Protects against tetanus, diphtheria, and pertussis (whooping cough).

Meningococcal Vaccines: A two-dose series of MenACWY is recommended, with a booster at age 16. MenB vaccine is recommended for some adolescents, especially those with certain health conditions or in outbreak situations.
HPV Vaccine: Recommended for both boys and girls, typically starting at age 11 or 12.
Annual Influenza (Flu) Vaccine: Protects against seasonal influenza.
Catch-up Vaccines: Adolescents who missed earlier vaccinations should also catch up on vaccines like Hepatitis A, Hepatitis B, polio, MMR (measles, mumps, and rubella), and chickenpox.

list.title: Protection from serious diseases:
list.snippet: These vaccines protect adolescents from potentially debilitating or life-threatening illnesses.

list.title: Reduced risk of outbreaks:
list.snippet: Vaccination helps prevent the spread of these diseases within communities, including schools and universities.

list.title: Protection for vulnerable individuals:
list.snippet: Adolescents can transmit diseases to infants, the elderly, and individuals with weakened immune systems, making vaccination crucial for community protection.

list.title: College requirements:
list.snippet: Many colleges and universities require specific vaccinations for enrollment.

list.title: Individual health conditions:
list.snippet: Some adolescents may need additional vaccines based on their medical history or other risk factors.

text_blocks.snippet: It's important to consult with a healthcare provider to ensure adolescents are up-to-date on all recommended vaccinations.
